human_name: IGHG4 single-copy locus carrying chimdup-PSV haplotype

GRCh38.note: single IGHG4 CH1 — no tandem dup, no NAHR block, but carries DUP_fixed PSV pattern

architecture_note: This entry is intentionally NOT a SegDup in the strict Bailey/Eichler sense — it is a SINGLE-COPY haplotype that carries the chimdup-PSV pattern at CH1 (pos 69 + 252 ALT alleles). Architectural classification is 'unresolved' because no second copy exists in the assembly. Most likely origin: gene-conversion from a chimdup haplotype, or a tandem-dup that lost one copy historically. Catalogued because LLmap needs to be able to distinguish this from canonical-PSV NoDup.

discriminating_snps.expected_pattern_in_carriers: ALT allele on the single IGHG4 copy
discriminating_snps.source: DNA-Architecture 104-sample sweep — 39/157 NoDup-haps carry this ALT

discriminating_snps.expected_pattern_in_carriers: ALT allele on the single IGHG4 copy

diagnostic_features.snp_density_note: Single-copy IGHG4 carrying the chimdup-PSV haplotype. 39/157 NoDup-haps in the 104-sample sweep show this pattern (24.8 % of all NoDup haps). Likely arose from gene-conversion of a previously-tandem-dup locus or from intra-pangenome haplotype exchange.

promoter_signature.note: Promoter signature is the chimdup variant — this is what makes the haplotype 'chimeric' even though the copy count is 1
